Quadrature partner of the SPM canonical HRF

Source: R/hrf-quadrature.R
hrf_spmg1_quadrature.Rd

The Hilbert transform of the SPM canonical HRF ([hrf_spmg1()]) on `[0, span]`, made orthogonal to the canonical HRF and scaled to the same L2 norm. Together the two functions form a quadrature pair: a small shift of the response in time acts, to a good approximation, as a rotation of the two coefficients, so their length carries amplitude and their angle carries latency. The temporal derivative in [HRF_SPMG2] plays the same role but only for shifts of about a second.

Usage

hrf_spmg1_quadrature(t, P1 = 5, P2 = 15, A1 = 1/120, span = 32)

Arguments

t

A vector of time points.

P1

The first exponent parameter (default: 5).

P2

The second exponent parameter (default: 15). The undershoot is t^P2 * exp(-t) / (6 * factorial(P2)), one sixth of a gamma density with shape P2 + 1 and unit rate.

A1

Amplitude scaling factor for the positive gamma function component; normally fixed at 1/120

span

Length in seconds of the window on which the function is defined (default 32). It is zero outside `[0, span]`.

Value

A numeric vector the same length as `t`.

Details

The function is tabulated once per parameter set on a 0.01 s grid (the Hilbert transform is computed with a zero-padded FFT) and interpolated linearly. Unlike the canonical HRF, the Hilbert transform of a causal function is not causal, so the quadrature partner does not start at zero: restricted to `[0, span]` it begins at about -0.37 of the canonical peak. Treat it as a companion regressor for estimating latency, not as a response shape.

References

Saad, Z. S., Ropella, K. M., Cox, R. W., & DeYoe, E. A. (2001). Analysis and use of FMRI response delays. *Human Brain Mapping*, 13(2), 74-93. doi:10.1002/hbm.1026

See also

[HRF_SPMGQ], [amplitude_latency()]

Other hrf_functions: hrf_basis_lwu(), hrf_boxcar(), hrf_bspline(), hrf_gamma(), hrf_gaussian(), hrf_inv_logit(), hrf_lwu(), hrf_mexhat(), hrf_sine(), hrf_spmg1(), hrf_time(), hrf_weighted()

Examples

t <- seq(0, 32, by = 0.1)
h <- hrf_spmg1(t)
q <- hrf_spmg1_quadrature(t)
matplot(t, cbind(h, q), type = "l", lty = 1, ylab = "response")

sum(h * q)              # orthogonal
#> [1] -2.729261e-07
sum(h^2) / sum(q^2)     # equal norm
#> [1] 0.9984316
